purpose: Additive source-backed shared-workbench player/usables questions; frozen32/PLAY12/challenge157 remain untouched. Source and actual qualification are separate.

questions.query: Can I use the seven player playground actors and physical usables beside the flyers in the shared painting workbench?
facts: All eight flyers and seven player presets are offered in Pilot/Place model; five mechanical players retain articulated Rapier assemblies, while Dust Devil and Undertow use native material fields.
A passive barrel remains placeable. Up to eight logical actors share the canvas, with 64 physical owners and 64 rectangle proxies.
The five mechanical players can select the 32 existing physical usables; flyers and material fields have no equipment mount.
This source successor consumes unmerged #402 over merged #394 and is not owner gameplay acceptance or issue completion.

questions.query: How do eight logical workbench actors relate to 64 rigid bodies, compound proxies, part_index and granular response budgets?
facts: Eight actors may contain up to eight articulated parts each, within 64 physical owners and 64 total native rectangle proxies.
Independent bodies have unique physical ids and (instance_id,part_index) tuples; omitted legacy part defaults to zero and duplicate tuples refuse.
One independent body owns its mass/inertia/budget/application fence; compound Scooper proxies share one body rather than multiplying its budget.
Support observations share wrench age/geometry admission; fixed equipment cannot be moved by correction, and an ownership-mode change retires old samples.

questions.query: Does Shift still slide the Acrobat and brake the bike after moving player playground controls into the workbench?
facts: Mechanical/material players retain Shift secondary while flyers keep Shift boost and Ctrl brake.
Actor options saves per-model keyboard bindings; brackets select models, Tab cycles instances and number keys remain reserved.
Mechanical movement impulse/body torque multipliers do not retune built-in wheel/joint motors; native fields accept bindings only.
Flyer boost/throttle response/side swap/emission controls do not acquire meanings for unsupported player capabilities.

questions.query: Do native Sand cloud and Water blob players in the workbench create another World, teleport cells or refill when reset?
facts: Material players call the existing native field in the exclusive worker-owned workbench World; no standalone extra World or fake Rapier body is created.
A new explicit placement attempts a 256-cell seed into empty unmasked locations, reporting insertion/refusal; retained resets and peer edits do not replenish it.
Reset/move changes the control centre and retires input without moving, erasing or recreating cells; removing a field leaves native material behind.
The field selects matching local material rather than persistent parcel identities, follows the centroid at most four cells/tick, and has a six-tick issued-observation lease.

questions.query: How do I use, drop and recover physical equipment without accidentally painting, and what must survive a workbench settings change?
facts: Choose a mechanical player, usable and power, then wait for ordinary play/step acknowledgement while held equipment is available.
Use equipment routes pointer trigger/alternate; Paint routes brush input; M uses, N drops and U attempts local clear-path reattachment.
Graph changes use bounded runtime custody/refusal instead of silently refilling charge, duplicating dropped chassis or deleting committed payloads.
Inventory, recipe and conservation semantics stay in the existing usable owner; a material-field actor or flyer has no equipment topology.

questions.query: Does workbench setup version 4 save live player articulation, charge and projectiles, or just the initial actor and usable recipe?
facts: Version 4 stores explicit actor definitions/spawns/tuning plus initial usable_index -1..31 and usable_power 0..1.
Valid versions 2/3 migrate with preserved options, neutral missing controls and empty equipment.
Starting recipes do not resume live motion, tool charge, projectiles or processor stock; runtime graph custody is a different mechanism.
Keyboard bindings remain private model preferences rather than serialized map content.
